title: Fugaro models search
description: The document `fugaro models search <text> --json` prints: the hits of an offline search of this binary's built-in provider price catalog and its embedded Claude table, by a substring of the model ID, beside the models the owner's own model_prices prices. One object per row the read prints, in the same order, with a price carried as the range the row is charged over rather than as the cell the read formats. The search reaches nothing: what it says is what this binary's own tables and the selected project config already say. Members are only ever added within a version (D784), so a renamed or re-meant member is a new member under a new name and the old one is kept, and removing or retyping one bumps version. No object here is closed for that reason: additionalProperties is left true everywhere, because a consumer that refused a member this schema does not know would refuse a newer CLI's document, which D784 promises to keep readable under the same version.

query.description: The term the search was given, as the caller wrote it. It is data: a control character in it is escaped by the JSON encoding rather than the terminal's own escaping.

models.description: One object per hit, in the order the read prints them: the catalog's tiers, the embedded Claude table's rows, then the models the owner's own model_prices prices, each set in ID order. Empty on a miss, never absent.

id.description: The model ID, as the table that carries the row spells it. It is data: a control character in it is escaped by the JSON encoding and read back as the bytes the table holds.

source.description: Where the row's price comes from: this binary's Claude table, the built-in provider price catalog, or the owner's model_prices. Nothing else is a hit: a model with no price is a miss, which the read answers with the one way to price it.

tier.description: The catalog tier the price is over: the ZDR-eligible endpoints, or every endpoint the model is served by. Absent on a row that has no tier — the embedded table's and the owner's own.

input_per_m.description: The input price range, US dollars per million tokens. Absent on a dimension the tier prices no endpoint for, and never written as a zero (D7(a)); the two ends are equal on a row that has a single price.

output_per_m.description: The output price range, US dollars per million tokens. Absent on a dimension the tier prices no endpoint for.

endpoints.description: How many endpoints the model is served by. Absent on a row the catalog does not price, which is every row whose source is not catalog.

zdr_endpoints.description: How many of those endpoints are ZDR-eligible, and the read's ENDPOINTS column shows `N of M endpoints` out of this and endpoints. Written even where the count is 0 — a model whose endpoints are none of them ZDR-eligible carries a real 0 — and absent only on a row the catalog does not price, which is a different thing.

route.description: The route of the selected project that claims the model — the provider whose models claim it, or `direct` for a Claude ID nothing routes. Empty is a model no route of this project serves, which a launch refuses and the read prints as `no route`.

context_tokens.description: The context the model accepts, as the catalog or the embedded table reports it. Absent when the row's table reports none.

max_output_tokens.description: The output the model accepts, as the catalog or the embedded table reports it. Absent when the row's table reports none.

min.description: The cheapest end of the range: one endpoint of the row's tier prices it.

max.description: The dearest end of the range. Equal to min on a row that has a single price, and never above it: the catalog's loader refuses a max below its min.
